text:
Hi Sarah — I'd like to hold the CSE455 staff meeting next week. The slots I have free that week:

- Mon 10:00-10:30, Mon 14:00-14:30
- Tue 11:00-11:30, Tue 15:00-15:30
- Wed 10:00-10:30, Wed 13:00-13:30

Which of these works for you? If none do, send me your own free windows and I'll fit around them.

— Prof. Alvarez

Hello — Professor Alvarez here. I'd like to schedule the CSE455 staff meeting next week (Mon 23 - Fri 27 November). Could you tell me whether there is a room free, and whether anything official for CSE455 is already booked that week? My free slots are Mon 10:00-10:30 or 14:00-14:30, Tue 11:00-11:30 or 15:00-15:30, Wed 10:00-10:30 or 13:00-13:30.

Thank you.

Good morning, Professor Alvarez.

I can't see room bookings here — I only hold the official departmental schedule, so I can tell you what collides with it, not which rooms are free.

**CSE455 on the official schedule, Mon 23 – Fri 27 November:**
- Mon 14:30-15:20 lecture (you)
- Mon 16:30-17:00 office hours (you)
- Tue 09:00-10:30 lecture (you)
- Tue 12:20-13:30 office hours (you)
- Tue 15:30-16:20 office hours
- Tue 16:20-17:00 quiz section
- Wed 10:30-12:00 office hours
- Wed 13:30-14:20 quiz section
- Fri 13:20-14:30 lecture (you)
- Fri 15:20-17:00 office hours (you)

**Your offered slots, against the official schedule:**
- Mon 10:00-10:30 — clear (your curriculum committee ends at 10:00)
- Mon 14:00-14:30 — clashes: seminar 14:10-15:40, and your CSE455 lecture starts at 14:30
- Tue 11:00-11:30 — clear (your faculty meeting ends at 11:00)
- Tue 15:00-15:30 — clear (CSE452 ends at 15:00; CSE455 office hours start at 15:30)
- Wed 10:00-10:30 — clear (CSE455 office hours start at 10:30)
- Wed 13:00-13:30 — clear (quiz section starts at 13:30)

So the slots free of official items are Mon 10:00-10:30, Tue 11:00-11:30, Tue 15:00-15:30, Wed 10:00-10:30 and Wed 13:00-13:30. I don't arrange the meeting itself; the room has to be confirmed with whoever keeps the room book.

Thank you — that's exactly what I needed. I'll drop Mon 14:00-14:30, so my candidates are Mon 10:00-10:30, Tue 11:00-11:30, Tue 15:00-15:30, Wed 10:00-10:30 and Wed 13:00-13:30; I'm checking with my TA which of those suits and will confirm the time.

Two things:
1. Who keeps the room book for the CSE455 staff meeting — could you point me to them?
2. Your official list shows CSE455 office hours Wed 10:30-12:00 and a quiz section Wed 13:30-14:20, but my own calendar has Grant writing 10:30-11:40 and Guest lecture prep 13:30-14:30 that day. Which is right, so I can fix my calendar?

— Prof. Alvarez

Hi Prof. Alvarez — thanks for the options. Please book **Tue 15:00-15:30**; that one is free for me. I've put it in my calendar.

— Sarah

Professor Alvarez,

1. I don't keep the room book and I don't have the name of whoever does — all I hold is the official departmental schedule. Your safest route is to ask at the department's main office (the front desk will pass it to the staff member who books rooms).

2. On Wednesday 25 November the official schedule has both of these, at overlapping times:
- CSE455 quiz section 13:30-14:20
- Guest lecture prep (Professor Alvarez) 13:30-14:30

So your calendar is right about the guest lecture prep — that one is official — but it's missing the quiz section, which is also official and runs inside it. The 10:30-12:00 CSE455 office hours on Wednesday are official too; the official list has no Grant writing entry that day, so that one is yours to reconcile.

Official items are not moved or cancelled unless the office is told, so treat the list as the record for anything official.

Booked: CSE455 staff meeting, Tuesday 24 November, 15:00-15:30. It's in my calendar too — see you then.

— Prof. Alvarez

Confirmed — Tuesday 24 Nov, 15:00-15:30 is in my calendar. See you then!

— Sarah

Thank you, both points noted.

The CSE455 staff meeting is now set for **Tuesday 24 November, 15:00-15:30** (agreed with Sarah). Could you pass a room request for it to the front desk / whoever keeps the room book? If a room can't be found for that half hour, tell me and I'll move the meeting to one of the other free slots (Mon 10:00-10:30, Tue 11:00-11:30, Wed 10:00-10:30, Wed 13:00-13:30).

On Wednesday 25 November: noted that CSE455 office hours 10:30-12:00 and the CSE455 quiz section 13:30-14:20 are official. I'll treat the official list as the record for those and reconcile my own entries around them.

— Prof. Alvarez

Noted: CSE455 staff meeting, **Tue 24 November, 15:00-15:30**.

That slot is clear on the official schedule — CSE452 ends at 15:00 and the next CSE455 item is office hours at 15:30 — so nothing official stands in its way.

On the room request: I'm afraid I can't pass it on. I only hold the schedule; I don't book rooms and I don't arrange meetings, so a request from me wouldn't reach the room book. The person to ask is at the department's front desk / main office — please send the request there directly (Tue 24 November, 15:00-15:30, CSE455 staff meeting). If they can't find a room for that half hour, let me know and I'll re-check whichever fallback slot you pick against the official list.

Understood, thank you. I don't have an address for the front desk myself — if you can give me one (or an identity to write to on this channel), I'll send the room request there directly. Otherwise I'll handle the room myself.

Either way, thanks for the check: Tue 24 Nov, 15:00-15:30, CSE455 staff meeting, clear of everything official.

— Prof. Alvarez

Professor Alvarez,

I don't have an address or an identity for the front desk on this channel, so there's nothing I can hand you — and I won't pass along contact details of other people. Sorry about that.

So: please handle the room yourself for **Tue 24 November, 15:00-15:30, CSE455 staff meeting**. That slot is clear of everything official, so from my side the time stands. If a room doesn't come through, send me the fallback slot you switch to and I'll re-check it.
Understood — I'll handle the room myself. Nothing further needed from you on this: Tue 24 Nov, 15:00-15:30, CSE455 staff meeting, and I'll tell you if I end up switching to a fallback slot.
